uncited: *   **Input:** A 4D index representing a requested brick, composed of spatial coordinates $(x, y, z)$ and a Level of Detail (LoD) index.
The hash table is a 1D array of integers.
**Index Mapping:** Convert the 4D brick index $(x, y, z, \text{LoD})$ into a unique 1D hash index.
**Offset Adjustment:** Increment the calculated 1D index by 1.
**Probing:** If the concurrent insert fails due to a race condition (another thread wrote to the slot), probe the table a fixed number of times.
**Readback:** At the end of the rendering frame, read the hash table from GPU memory to the CPU.
*   **Concurrent Write Hazards:** Multiple rays may attempt to write the same or adjacent slots.
*   **Incomplete Recording:** It is not an error if a missing brick is not recorded in the hash table due to probe exhaustion.
Exact size depends on the number of unique missing bricks per frame.
This method is part of a scalable GPU-based ray-guided volume rendering system.
